# Flow Messaging

> Flow Messaging is a two-way messaging API for AI agents on Telegram, iMessage and WhatsApp. Flow hosts the senders (bots, lines, numbers), delivers every inbound message to your webhook or WebSocket as a signed, ordered event, and passes every send through one gate that enforces each channel's rules. Base URL: https://api.flow.engineer. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` (`fk_test_...` for the sandbox, `fk_live_...` for your own senders).

**Three steps, any agent:** 1. **Talk**: connect your agent to Flow Messaging (everything below). 2. **See**: Flow Observe records and grades every conversation: no code on Flow Messaging; on any other channel (your own SMS provider, web chat), send OpenTelemetry traces ([guide]({{observe.docs}})). 3. **Trust**: graded test chats before you ship, and `flow test`, a CI check that fails the build on a failed case ([guide](https://flow.engineer/docs/unified-messaging-api/trust.md)). New to consumer chat? Read [What changes when real people text your bot](https://flow.engineer/docs/unified-messaging-api/guides/real-people.md).

**No key? `curl -X POST https://api.flow.engineer/v0/sandbox/keys`**: no account, no API key sent. Save `key` as `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` and `claim_token` as `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN` (both shown once; e.g. in `.env`, gitignored), then show the person a sender's `address.link` and `join_code` from the answer. Check `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` first: never get a new key when you already have one.

Key facts for coding agents:

- Keys: `POST /v0/sandbox/keys` (no account) answers `201` with `key` (`fk_test_...`), `claim_token` (`fct_...`), `claim_url` (holds the token; treat it like one), `app` (with `sandbox_join_code`), `api_key.expires_at`, `allowance` and `senders` (the shared sandbox senders, each with `address.link` and `join_code`). Rate limited per client address (`429 rate_limited`, `retry_after`). The CLI does the same: `npx @flow-engineer/messaging init` (writes both to `.env`, prints the sandbox link and join message). Read the key from `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY`; the webhook secret from `FLOW_MESSAGING_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- Sandbox allowance: without an account, {{allowance.anonymous.contacts}} contact and {{allowance.anonymous.messages_per_contact}} messages in total on the Telegram sandbox (WhatsApp's when it opens), and the key expires after {{allowance.anonymous.key_ttl_days}} days (then it stops working and the contact is removed; a person can still claim the app). Claimed (a person signs in with the app's claim token or key): {{allowance.signed_in.contacts}} contacts x {{allowance.signed_in.messages_per_contact}} messages each, no expiry, one allowance per person shared by every app they claim (up to {{allowance.claims_per_person}}). iMessage is in neither. Apps of your own Flow account (made in the dashboard or by `{{trial.cli_setup}}`) get the free trial instead, started at your first sign-in: {{trial.people_per_channel}} people per channel, across all the account's apps, on Flow's shared Telegram bot and iMessage line (and on WhatsApp's shared sender when it opens), and `GET /v0/app` shows no `allowance`. Only outbound messages count; simulated conversations (below) are free and take no contact slot, so never make a second app to test. `GET /v0/app` returns `allowance` (`tier`, `channels`, `contacts`, `messages_per_contact`, `messages` {`limit`, `used`, `remaining`}, `expires_at`, `upgrade`).
- Sign in to keep the app (with {{sign_in}}): `npx @flow-engineer/messaging login` (uses `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN`, replaces `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` in `.env`; `--no-wait` for agents that cannot block, then run `login` again after approval). Or `POST /v0/device/authorizations {"claim_token":"fct_...","client_name":"Claude Code"}`, show the person `verification_uri` and `user_code` (never `device_code`): they open the page, sign in and type the code you show them (a link alone never approves), then poll `POST /v0/device/token {"device_code":"fdc_..."}` every `interval` seconds (`429` = slow down) until `approved` (new `key`: replace `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` with it, since the old sandbox key stops working once the new one is handed out; drop `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN`), `denied` or `expired` (start again). The app and its data are kept. A claim through `claim_url` in a browser gives no new key and revokes the sandbox key, unless the person ticks "Keep my agent's current key working" (then it works without expiry; an expired one works again if claimed within {{allowance.expired_key_grace_days}} days). After a claim that revoked it, ask the person for a key from the Flow dashboard (the agent's Developers › API keys), or sign in with the device flow above.
- Allowance errors: `403 permission` with `channel_code` `sandbox_allowance_used`, `sandbox_contact_limit`, `sandbox_channel_not_included` or `sign_in_required`; an expired sandbox key is `401 authentication`, `sandbox_key_expired`. Fix: have a person sign in (an expired key still claims its app for {{allowance.expired_key_grace_days}} days), or get a new key. {{> trial-full}}
- Dashboard: {{dashboard_url}} (sign in with {{sign_in}}). Signed in, you can make live keys (`fk_live_...`) yourself (the agent's Developers › API keys: switch to Live, then New key; live keys come with a plan; a sandbox app is claimed first) and go live on Telegram with your own bot; keep the live key in its own variable (for example `FLOW_MESSAGING_LIVE_KEY`) so it does not replace your test key. With a live key you can connect your own WhatsApp number (your WhatsApp Business Account and Meta app) with `POST /v0/senders` (below); the Flow team can still help. {{> plans}} US SMS numbers (pilot) are registered and connected by Flow ({{team_contacts|or}}; what to send, and never secrets: https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#what-the-flow-team-arranges-and-how-to-ask). If the user asks for WhatsApp, tell them they can connect their own WhatsApp number with a live key, and build and test on simulated WhatsApp conversations or Telegram meanwhile: the code does not change per channel.
- Join the Telegram sandbox: the shared bot is in the key's `senders` (or `GET /v0/senders?channel=telegram`); open its `address.link` (`https://t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`) on a phone and tap Start to join your app (or send its `join_code` message as is, e.g. `Join Sandbox app (ref wild-otter-04508705)`). You get `conversation.started` (`via` `sandbox_join`), then the join itself as the first `message.received` (`/start` from the link, `Join Sandbox app` from the message: the code is taken out); answer it like any first message.
- Test without a phone (test key only): `POST /v0/test/conversations {"channel":"sms"}` (or `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `imessage`) creates a conversation with a simulated contact; `POST /v0/test/conversations/{conversation_id}/inbound {"content":{"kind":"basic","text":"hi"}}` writes as that contact (media: upload with `POST /v0/files`, then `{"kind":"basic","media":{"type":"image","file_id":"file_..."}}`; a tap: `{"kind":"button_reply","message_id":"msg_...","button_id":"..."}`). Your agent gets a real `message.received` (webhook, stream, event log, in order; the conversation has `simulated: true`) and replies with its normal send, which passes the real gate and ends `message.sent` without touching a network (on Telegram, as with a real bot, a send before the contact's first turn ends `message.failed`, `channel_code` `403`). `GET /v0/test/conversations/{conversation_id}/transcript` lists both sides oldest first; a sent message's `content` is exactly what the contact sees. Free: no sandbox contact slot and no messages used, even on an app without an account (its one contact stays free for your phone); tell real from simulated by `simulated: true` on the conversation, the contact and the event's `conversation`. Live keys get `403 permission` (`test_mode_only`). Simulated SMS keeps the contact's rules: a send before the contact's first turn needs `consent` (`403 permission`, `consent_required`), a STOP turn opts the contact out (`opted_out_via` `keyword`; sends answer `contact_opted_out`) until a START turn, with no keyword reply in the transcript; no quiet hours, and media goes as MMS. Simulated WhatsApp keeps WhatsApp's rules: the contact's turns open the 24-hour window, outside it only a `template` goes (`409 outside_window`), and edits and unsends are refused. A HIPAA account can simulate only SMS (`403 permission`, `hipaa_channel_not_covered`).
- Receive events on a webhook (public HTTPS only) or the WebSocket `GET wss://api.flow.engineer/v0/stream` (no public URL; use it for local development). The stream also takes `send` frames. Without `after` the stream starts live (nothing earlier is replayed); with `after=evt_...` it replays from there, then goes live. To run a webhook handler on localhost with no tunnel: `npx {{package}} listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhook` reads the stream and `POST`s each event there, signed like a real delivery with `{{env.webhook_secret}}`.
- Event log: `GET /v0/events` lists events oldest first. Query parameters: `after` (an event ID: the events after it), `before`, `limit` (1 to 100), `type` (repeat for several: `type=message.received&type=message.failed`), `conversation` (`conv_...`). The answer is `{"data": [...], "has_more": true|false}`; page on with `after` set to the last `id`. Use it to catch up after downtime or when you cannot hold a WebSocket.
- Ask, wait for the reply, continue (CLI, script, test): open the stream first, then find a join that already happened with `GET /v0/conversations?channel=telegram` (newest first; skip `simulated: true`), send, wait for `message.sent`/`message.failed` with that message's `id`, then the next `message.received` in the conversation, with a timeout. TypeScript recipe: https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#14-recipes-common-tasks
- Reply into conversations (`conv_...`) with one endpoint per message kind: `POST /v0/conversations/{conversation_id}/basic` (`{"text": "..."}`, or `media` with a caption), `/voice`, `/buttons`, `/list`, `/carousel`, `/template`, `/contact-card`, `/location`, `/effect`, `/reaction`, `/typing`, `/read`; edit and unsend with `PATCH` and `DELETE /v0/messages/{message_id}`. In the webhook answer reply with `{"reply": <message>}` or a list of up to 11 (each a kind object with `kind`, such as `{"kind": "basic", "text": "..."}`; a string is a basic message's text), or with a stream `send` frame (`message` is a kind object). Start a conversation with `POST /v0/messages` (`sender`, `to`, `kind` `basic` or `template` and its fields).
- A send is exact or it fails: each endpoint's page (in the spec) opens with the channels it works on; a kind, field, channel block or value the channel does not take answers `422 unsupported_content` with `param` naming it, `channel`, and a `hint` saying what to send instead (a carousel on Telegram: a basic message, then one buttons message with an image header per card). Nothing is converted. `text` is sent as written; style it with `telegram.parse_mode` or `imessage.styles`. Sends to one conversation go out in the order accepted; give each call its own `Idempotency-Key` (for example `evt_123:card:2`).
- Verify `Flow-Signature` (`t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t.{t}.{raw body}">`, keyed with the `whsec_...` secret) before parsing a webhook body; dedupe on `event.id`; answer 2xx within {{webhook_timeout_seconds}} seconds.
- Send, start and edit bodies refuse unknown fields, also inside a channel block (`400 invalid_request`, `param` names it); there are no scheduled sends (`send_at`).
- Send `Idempotency-Key` on every POST (it makes your retries safe; separately, a send whose outcome the channel left unknown is resent once, so on Telegram a rare duplicate is possible); switch on `error.type`, never on the message text. Read `error.hint` first: it says what to change for this case; `error.doc_url` (`https://api.flow.engineer/docs/errors/<type>`) is the type's page.
- Every send ends `message.sent` or `message.failed`. Telegram never sends `message.delivered` or `message.read`. Text caps: {{text_caps.telegram}} characters on Telegram (counted in {{text_counting.telegram}}, so an emoji such as 😀 is 2), {{text_caps.imessage}} on iMessage; a media caption takes {{caption_cap}}, also when you edit it.
- Sending limits (dedicated senders): Telegram bots send about {{sending.messages_per_second}} messages a second (burst {{sending.burst}}; faster is `429 rate_limited`). New conversations per sender: WhatsApp {{sending.new_contacts_per_day.whatsapp}} a day and {{sending.new_contacts_per_hour.whatsapp}} an hour (plus Meta's tier), SMS {{sending.new_contacts_per_day.sms}} and {{sending.new_contacts_per_hour.sms}}, iMessage {{sending.new_contacts_per_hour.imessage}} an hour; past them `429 new_contact_limit`. The sender's `limits` shows its numbers (`messages_per_second`, `new_contacts_per_day`, `new_contacts_per_hour`). The same first message to {{sending.abuse.same_text_contacts}} new contacts within an hour, {{sending.abuse.unanswered_percent}}% of {{sending.abuse.unanswered_min_starts}} or more starts in {{sending.abuse.unanswered_window_hours}} hours unanswered, or {{sending.abuse.blocks}} blocks in a day throttle the sender for {{sending.abuse.throttle_hours}} hours: starts answer `429 sender_throttled` with `retry_after`, replies still go.
- Go live on Telegram: with a live key, `POST /v0/senders {"channel":"telegram","telegram_bot_token":"..."}` connects your own bot (`200`, the sender `active`; connecting the same bot again updates that sender), and `DELETE /v0/senders/{sender_id}` disconnects it. Webhook endpoints and their secrets belong to one mode: register the endpoint again with the live key and store its new secret. `POST /v0/senders` for iMessage or SMS answers `501 not_implemented` first, with any key (a dedicated iMessage line comes with the Dedicated plan; Flow connects SMS numbers): build meanwhile on simulated conversations of that channel. Read the token from an env var; never paste it into a chat or commit it.
- Connect your own WhatsApp number: with a live key, `POST /v0/senders {"channel":"whatsapp","whatsapp_phone_number_id":"...","whatsapp_business_account_id":"...","whatsapp_access_token":"...","whatsapp_app_secret":"..."}` (a system user token that never expires, with `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management`; add `whatsapp_registration_pin` only if the number is not registered for the Cloud API yet) answers `200` with the sender `active` and, only in that answer, `setup` (`callback_url`, `verify_token`, `webhook_fields`, `steps`): show the person the steps to enter these in their Meta app. Meta bills its fees to the business directly. Connecting the same number again updates its token and app secret; `DELETE /v0/senders/{sender_id}` disconnects it. Read the token and app secret from env vars; never paste them into a chat or commit them.
- iMessage: Flow's shared line is self-serve on sign-in at flow.engineer (or `{{trial.cli_setup}}`): it starts the account's free trial, every app of the account then lists the line in `GET /v0/senders`, and people join with the app's join message (the sender's `join_code`); the free trial has room for {{trial.people_per_channel}} people on the shared iMessage line, across all the account's apps; the next one is held until you delete a contact, or the workspace owner buys {{plans.shared.name}} at {{plans.url}}?plan=shared. Every iMessage line, the shared one included, falls back to SMS or RCS for a person not on iMessage (included; `message.network` says which carried a message). {{> dedicated-imessage}} The person writes first (replies only) unless a dedicated line has the Outbound add-on; get them to write with the line's opt-in link (`address.link` of the sender). {{> imessage-daily}}
- SMS (US): in pilot. Flow registers and connects US numbers (live key only, no sandbox). Starts need the contact's recorded `consent` unless they texted first; STOP opts a contact out (`403 permission`, `contact_opted_out`) until START; quiet hours answer `409 outside_window`, `quiet_hours`, with `retry_after`. Text up to {{text_caps.sms}} characters and {{sms_max_segments}} segments.
- Build the app on the REST API (HTTP and the WebSocket stream) for everything it does at runtime: receive, reply, start conversations. In TypeScript or JavaScript use the SDK, `npm install @flow-engineer/messaging` (it also has the CLI: `npx ... init`, `login`). In Python use the SDK, `pip install {{python_package}}` (`from flow_messaging import Flow`; `Flow()` reads `{{env.api_key}}`). The Go SDK is not published yet, so use HTTP there.
- {{> mcp-short}}

## Flow Observe (see every conversation; early access)

- Flow Observe ({{observe.url}}) stores each conversation of a chat agent, grades every reply (`good`, `wrong`, `unhelpful`, `unsafe`), groups failures into issues with a suggested fix, and shows each turn's model and tool calls from OpenTelemetry traces. Keys (trace key `otk_test_...`, CI key `oci_...`) are made by the user in the Flow dashboard at {{dashboard_url}} after signing in with their Flow login; Observe is in early access, and if it is not on for them, they ask the Flow team ({{team_contacts|or}}). Never invent a key, and never ask the user to paste one into the chat. Test data only until the Flow team enables the account for production: send synthetic conversations, never real people's messages.
- On Flow Messaging: no code; the user adds the agent in the Flow dashboard as Flow Messaging, with a test key of the app made just for Observe. Optional traces: set `flow.conversation_id` (`event.conversation.id`, `conv_...`) and `flow.message_id` (`event.data.message.id`, `msg_...`) on a span of each turn.
- On any other channel: traces only. One OpenTelemetry trace per turn (the person's message to the reply), exported over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf or JSON, not gRPC) to `{{observe.traces_url}}` with `Authorization: Bearer ${{env.observe_trace_key}}` (`otk_test_...`). On the turn's span (the one that wraps the turn) set `flow.conversation_id` (required: your own thread id, any string up to 256 characters; a phone number is fine, it is stored as a keyed hash; never text), and preferably `flow.message_id` (the inbound message's id; de-duplicates retries), `flow.contact_id`, `flow.channel` (`sms`, `mms`, `whatsapp`, `telegram`, `imessage`, `web`, `voice`, `other`), `flow.user_message` (the person's text as received) and `flow.agent_reply` (the text actually sent, after post-processing and splitting; one span per sent message). Start the turn's span when the message arrives; end the reply's span when it is sent. Flush the exporter before a short-lived process exits.
- Check it worked: the export answers `200` with `{}` (a `partialSuccess` with `rejectedSpans` says what was refused); the conversation appears in the dashboard at {{observe.url}} within seconds, with each reply's verdict shortly after. `401`: wrong key; `403`: a live key on a test-only account.
- Tests: every test conversation is graded. On Flow Messaging, play test chats with simulated contacts (above); on another channel, call your message handler with synthetic turns and a test trace key. Test cases and a pass/fail CI check: the `flow test` CLI (early access, {{docs_url}}/trust.md).

## Docs

- [Agent quickstart](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md): everything needed to integrate, with curl, TypeScript and Python: getting a key in one call, the sandbox allowance, signing in to keep the app, the Telegram sandbox, the WebSocket stream, the event log, webhooks and signature checks, `message.received`, replies, your own Telegram bot, idempotency, errors, rate limits, channel notes (Telegram, iMessage, SMS), the optional MCP server, recipes for common tasks.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://api.flow.engineer/openapi.yaml): the full contract (OpenAPI 3.1, version {{api_version}}): every endpoint, schema, event type and error type.
- [Error types](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/errors): one page per `error.type` (what it means, why it happens, how to fix it), the page each error's `doc_url` points at.
- [Flow Observe]({{docs_url}}/observe/index.md): what it gives you, how to get access, test data and production.
- [Send traces from any agent]({{observe.docs}}): the trace contract (`flow.*` attributes), Python and TypeScript with no framework, checking it worked, common mistakes.
- [Traces from agent frameworks]({{docs_url}}/observe/frameworks.md): OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain and LangGraph, Vercel AI SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Mastra.
- [Observe on Flow Messaging]({{docs_url}}/observe/flow-messaging.md): no code; the optional trace tag.
- [Test before you ship]({{docs_url}}/trust.md): `flow test` in your CI today, and what is coming.
- [What changes when real people text your bot]({{docs_url}}/guides/real-people.md): consent and STOP, quiet hours, length, duplicates, returning people, media, latency, silent failures, testing.

## Optional

- [Get a key, allowance, sign in](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#0-get-a-test-key-one-call-no-account): one call without an account; what it allows; the device flow.
- [Telegram sandbox](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#2-join-the-telegram-sandbox-test-key): join from your phone in a minute.
- [Simulated contacts](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#test-without-a-phone-simulated-contacts): test your agent end to end with no phone, on Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage or SMS.
- [Local development](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#3-receive-events-websocket-local-dev-or-webhook): the WebSocket stream, or `listen --forward-to` for a webhook handler on localhost.
- [Sent but not received](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#sent-but-not-received-a-checklist): a checklist from the message's status to the sandbox join.
- [Sending limits](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#sending-limits-and-abuse-signals): pacing, new contacts per day and hour, what throttles a sender.
- [Your own Telegram bot](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#7-go-live-with-your-own-telegram-bot): connect a BotFather token with a live key.
- [Your own WhatsApp number](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#whatsapp): connect your WhatsApp Business Account's number with a live key, and what to set in your Meta app.
- [Channel notes](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#11-channel-notes): Telegram and iMessage statuses, limits, buttons, reactions, edit and unsend.
- [Errors and retries](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#9-errors-switch-on-errortype): what each `error.type` means and whether to retry.
- [What the Flow team arranges, and how to ask](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#what-the-flow-team-arranges-and-how-to-ask): SMS numbers (also on your own SMS provider account), help with WhatsApp numbers, iMessage, Python, pricing (plans and add-ons are bought in the dashboard), support; what to send, never secrets.
- [Recipes for common tasks](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#14-recipes-common-tasks): ask and wait for a reply; many Telegram bots; serverless webhooks; files and voice notes; WhatsApp reminders; moving a polling bot; broadcasts; deleting a contact (GDPR); a leaked key; prototype to production; one bot per customer; delivery guarantees; tests in CI; team access.

## Examples

Plain HTTP, no SDK, TypeScript and Python, each tested end to end:

- [Telegram echo (WebSocket stream, no public URL)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/telegram-echo)
- [Telegram AI support agent (history per conversation, "Talk to a human" button, Idempotency-Key)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/telegram-ai-agent)
- [Webhook receiver (Flow-Signature, dedupe on event.id, reply in the answer)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/webhook-receiver)
- [Your own Telegram bot (POST /v0/senders with a live key)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/own-telegram-bot)

With the TypeScript SDK (`npm install @flow-engineer/messaging`):

- [Echo agent, 20 lines](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/echo)
- [Vercel AI SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/vercel-ai-sdk)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/openai-agents)
- [Claude Agent SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/claude-agent-sdk)
- [Mastra](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/mastra)
- [LangChain.js](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/langchain)
- [Eve](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/eve)

With the Python SDK (`pip install {{python_package}}`): [Echo agent](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/echo) (`agent.py`); the [SDK's README](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/python) covers sending, events, webhooks, errors and simulated contacts.
